The diff makes that statement wrong, and in the direction that loses data. `getResult` (line 302) now documents that its `error.Closed` has three causes: the drained terminal state, a stale wake on an open queue, and a `close` that raced in while operations are still in flight. `wait` never returns `error.Closed` in the last two cases; it blocks and delivers the in-flight completions. So a select driver that follows the header, and copies the dispatcher example above it (`error.Closed => break`), breaks out of its loop while `pending` is non-empty. Those completions are then never handed out, and for a heap-backed dispatcher (the ownership rule stated at lines 12-20) their memory is never freed. The header is the only place a user reads the protocol from, and it never names `isDrained`: the new predicate is documented only on itself and inside `getResult`, where a caller has no reason to look. The header must state the second difference and point the select driver at `isDrained()`."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 392, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "New public `isDrained` has no test, including the closed-but-not-drained case it exists for", "body": "`isDrained` is new public API and nothing in the test block below exercises it. The case it was added for is the one with no coverage: the queue is closed while an operation is still in flight, the select arm reports `error.Closed`, and `isDrained()` must answer `false` so the driver keeps draining. The nearest existing test, `close over an in-flight operation does not wake a parked select` (line 1246), already builds exactly that state and asserts only the select result, so it would pass unchanged if `isDrained` returned `self.closed`, which the doc comment names as the wrong answer for this case. Nothing pins the terminal answer either (`true` only after the last completion is taken), nor the `false` on an open empty queue that the stale-wake path depends on. Add assertions on `isDrained()` at those three points, so a later change to the predicate cannot go green."}]}
